note: no narration; beats derive from frame-count timing in source. All scheduling is frame-based at fr = 30 fps (src/globals.js: frames(sec) = round(30*sec)). Graph01 defines t.start = frames(2) = 60, t.txt = frames(5) = 150, t.trace = frames(14.7) = 441. Graph_BFS.show() advances a state machine every this.f = 52 frames (~1.73 s) once its frame counter fc exceeds 441 and fc % 52 === 0, so the first algorithm step lands at fc = 468 (~15.6 s) and each subsequent state transition at +52 frames. Edge set is randomized per run (randomizeEdges(EU, 0.47)), so loop length and end times vary; estimates for the loop/finish beats are approximate against the 103 s video and the recorded run.

beats.title: Graph draws itself in (nodes then edges, staggered)
beats.whatChanges: 19 Node circles fade/grow in, start times staggered across frames(1.7) (start + frames(1.7)*i/n); ~33 randomly chosen Edge lines grow in over 0.8 s each, similarly staggered. Node labels are blanked to " " by Graph_BFS so vertices start unnumbered.
beats.invariant: Vertex positions (hard-coded triangular-lattice coordinates in G.V) never move for the rest of the video.

beats.title: BFS pseudocode types itself in beside the graph
beats.whatChanges: Title 'Breadth-first search' (Yellow) then five pseudocode lines write in one character per frame; each line's start = previous start + str.length + 17 frames, so pacing is proportional to text length (a stand-in for narration pace).
beats.invariant: Pseudocode text, once written, stays on screen verbatim for the entire video; only the Tracer arrow moves against it.

beats.title: State 0: enqueue start vertex 0
beats.whatChanges: Tracer arrow points at line 'Create a queue, and enqueue start vertex'; vertex 0 recolors to Yellow (= in queue) and its BFS number '0' fades in via a fresh TextFade.
beats.invariant: queue = [0], visited = {0}; all other vertices remain unnumbered Blue.

beats.title: States 1–2 alternate: dequeue vertex, absorb its unvisited neighbors
beats.whatChanges: Every 52 frames (~1.73 s) one transition fires. State 1: arrow moves to 'Dequeue a vertex from queue' and the front-of-queue node pulses with an Orange arc-sweep highlight. State 2: arrow moves to 'Add its unvisited neighbors to queue'; the dequeued node turns Green (done), each incident edge to an unvisited neighbor flashes Orange, and each neighbor turns Yellow and receives its BFS order number (TextFade starts staggered +4 frames apart so numbers pop in sequence).
beats.invariant: Queue discipline: bottom index only increments, top only increments, so numbering equals dequeue-independent BFS order. visited[] only ever gains members; a Green node never changes color again; layer-by-layer frontier expansion is visible as Yellow ring growing outward from vertex 0.

beats.title: State 4 (conditional): restart BFS at an unvisited vertex
beats.whatChanges: If the queue empties while unvisited vertices remain (possible because edges are random), the arrow returns to the enqueue line and the lowest-index unvisited vertex is enqueued, numbered, and turned Yellow. Occurs zero or more times per run; timing depends on the random edge set of the recorded run.
beats.invariant: Same queue/visited discipline; previously finished (Green) vertices are untouched.

beats.title: State 3: End
beats.whatChanges: Arrow moves to 'End'; the last dequeued vertex recolors Green; this.finished = true stops the state machine while the final frame keeps rendering. (Video runs 103 s; the tail past this beat is the held final frame plus the brief spoken outro whisper caught.)
beats.invariant: All 19 vertices Green and numbered 0..18 in BFS order; the entire pseudocode, graph, and numbering remain on screen.
